slot.brief: For a given 3d-series ion, write the d-electron configuration, count unpaired electrons and compute the spin-only magnetic moment.

stem: For a gaseous high-spin $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ ion, which row gives its $3d$ configuration, number of unpaired electrons and spin-only magnetic moment?

verdicts.working: Fe²⁺ has a 3d⁶ configuration. High-spin d⁶ has 4 unpaired electrons, so μ = √[4(4 + 2)] = √24 ≈ 4.90 BM.

working:
$\text{Fe}^{2+}: [\text{Ar}]3d^6$.
High-spin $3d^6$ has $n=4$ unpaired electrons.
$\mu_{\text{so}}=\sqrt{n(n+2)}=\sqrt{4(6)}=\sqrt{24}=4.90\ \text{BM}$.

Independent check: Fe²⁺ has a 3d⁶ configuration. High-spin d⁶ has 4 unpaired electrons, so μ = √[4(4 + 2)] = √24 ≈ 4.90 BM.
solution:
$\text{Fe}^{2+}$ has configuration $[\text{Ar}]3d^6$. In the high-spin state, $3d^6$ has $n=4$ unpaired electrons.
$$\mu_{\mathrm{so}}=\sqrt{n(n+2)}=\sqrt{4(6)}=\sqrt{24}=4.90\ \text{BM}$$
